extracted.intended_audience: senior biomedical researchers at U.S. research institutions considering applying to the HHMI Investigator Program
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and selection criteria for the HHMI Investigator national competition, which appoints individual scientists (not projects) to long-term, flexible investigator positions. Emphasizes creativity, risk-taking, interdisciplinary approaches, tool development, and potential for significant contributions to basic biomedical research.

rubrics_metrics.name: People, not projects (selection philosophy)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI selects and supports people rather than awarding grants for specific research projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program seeks researchers who will be given long-term, flexible funding to pursue ideas and change direction as needed; emphasis is on the individual’s potential rather than a fixed project plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity and productivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators are 'widely known for their creativity and productivity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHMI looks for scientists who have demonstrated a track record of creative, productive research — individuals who push the bounds of knowledge in biomedical research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to take risks and explore unproven avenues
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates should be willing to take risks, explore unproven avenues, and embrace uncertainty or the chance of failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Institute encourages high‑risk, potentially high‑reward science and values researchers who pursue bold directions even when outcomes are uncertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursuit of significant biological questions with rigor and depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators identify and pursue significant biological questions in a rigorous and deep manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection favors work centered on important biological problems, approached with methodological rigor and depth of inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of new tools and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators develop new tools and methods that enable creative experimental approaches to biological questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHMI values methodological innovation and tool-building that open new ways to address biological problems; candidates who create enabling technologies are favored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary approaches and cross-disciplinary transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates may bring to bear concepts or techniques from other disciplines (e.g., biophysics, chemical biology, computational biology, engineering).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Institute seeks investigators who integrate ideas or methods across disciplines to enable novel experimental strategies or conceptual advances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking basic biology and medicine
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators forge links between basic biology and medicine, opening new pathways for disease diagnosis and drug discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While focused on basic science, HHMI values work that has clear potential to inform medical applications or translational directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breadth of acceptable disciplines (inclusivity of fields)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI supports investigators across many biomedical disciplines and adjacent fields, including plant sciences, evolutionary biology, and patient-oriented research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program explicitly includes diverse fields (genetics, cell biology, developmental biology, biochemistry, neuroscience, biophysics, chemical biology, biomedical engineering, computational biology, etc.), and has partnered programs (e.g., HHMI‑GBMF) to encourage underfunded fields like plant science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential for large contributions to science and society (impact)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI seeks researchers whose work could result in large contributions to science and society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference is given to research directions that have the potential for transformative impact, including societal benefits and significant advances in understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative, large‑scope, transformative team projects (HCIA criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI Collaborative Innovation Awards support interdisciplinary teams led by an HHMI investigator to pursue potentially transformative projects that are new and large in scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HCIA projects should be interdisciplinary, require a range of expertise, be potentially transformative, and justify funding for collaborators over a multi‑year period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host institution arrangement and continued institutional participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators are based at host institutions across the U.S. and continue to participate in educational and administrative activities at their hosts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be affiliated with eligible U.S. research institutions and be prepared to maintain ties and responsibilities at their host institutions while being HHMI investigators (with HHMI providing salary, benefits, and research budget).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment term and renewal expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Appointment is for a seven‑year term, which may be renewed after an exacting review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates should be prepared for a term appointment model with performance/impact assessed at renewal; long‑term productivity and progress are relevant to continued appointment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility scope (who may apply)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI accepts applications from researchers at more than 200 research institutions across the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be based at eligible U.S. institutions (see 'Eligible Institutions' download); the competition is national in scope.
